Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of NorthStar's vendor evaluation we're consolidating detailed answers to our Support & Customer Success section (TAM coverage, escalation paths, on-call hours, incident communication templates and expected turnaround times). I've attached the RFP worksheet with the specific items we need filled.

- A clear TAM coverage matrix (roles, hours, SLA targets for P1/P2).
- Example incident communications for a P1 and a P2 (initial ack, updates cadence, postmortem).
- Escalation path showing who we contact inside Redwood at each severity.

Can you confirm you can return this by Friday? Also, if there are any items that require redlines or legal review, flag them early.

Regards,

NorthStar Financial

Rafael — attaching draft responses. I completed the coverage matrix and wrote the incident comms templates (P1 initial ack, P1 rolling updates, P2 initial ack + next steps, and a sample post-incident RCA outline).

Highlights / choices I made:
- TAM coverage: Primary TAM (M-F 6am-6pm PT) + Regional after-hours rotation for Sev1 (on-call list attached). For customers on Dedicated we offer a named TAM with 1-hour P1 response and 4-hour P2 response. Non-dedicated (hosted API) customers get a pooled TAM with 2-hour P1 response SLA and 8-hour P2 SLA; standard support hours are 6am–6pm PT M-F.
- Escalation steps: TAM -> Support Ops -> On-call SRE (in escalation matrix) -> VP CS for account-impacting incidents. Contacts are role-based, not personal, but I'll include role emails and pager links.
- Incident comms cadence for P1: initial ack within 15 minutes, updates every 60 minutes until mitigation, postmortem within 5 business days. For P2: ack within 1 hour, updates every 4 hours, postmortem within 10 business days.

I've flagged two RFP items where legal may want different wording around data residency and audit access — marked in the spreadsheet column 'legal_review_required'.

Attachments: NSF_RFP_Support_Responses_v1.xlsx, NorthStar_Incident_Templates.docx

Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:52:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP follow-up: Detailed CS/TAM questions and incident comms

Adding escalation diagram and suggested SLA table — see attached PDF. A couple of notes for Rafael before we send:

1) Escalation contacts: for enterprise customers we recommend including both role-based emails and a single exec escalation point (VP CS) — this reduces delays when people change.
2) Fallback policy: propose an automatic model-fallback to a broadly compatible variant (documented in the SLA) when Dedicated capacity constraints occur; this reduces total outage time and aligns with our graceful degradation approach.

If procurement pushes back on response times for hosted customers, offer an optional 'Priority Support' addon (monthly fee) that improves P1 to 30-minute response and assigns a named TAM.

Attachment: TAM_Coverage_Matrix.pdf

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks for the detailed worksheet. Attached are the completed responses and templates (NSF_RFP_Support_Responses_v1.xlsx, NorthStar_Incident_Templates.docx, TAM_Coverage_Matrix.pdf). Summary of what we provided below:

- TAM coverage: named TAM for Dedicated; pooled TAM for hosted with optional Priority Support addon. See matrix for hours, escalation roles, and pager links.
- SLAs: P1 (Dedicated) — 1 hour ack, 1 hour initial mitigation target, hourly updates; P1 (Hosted, Priority addon) — 30 minute ack; P1 (Hosted standard) — 2 hour ack. P2: 4 hour ack (Dedicated 1-4 hours depending on severity). Postmortem timelines and RCA ownership included.
- Escalation path: role-based escalation (TAM -> Support Ops -> On-call SRE -> VP CS); included exec escalation contact for account-impacting incidents.
- Incident comms: templates for initial ack, hourly update, and final RCA were provided; we also include suggested messaging for customer-facing status pages and legal notification triggers.

Two items flagged for legal: data residency audit access and persistent access logs for on-prem customers. We marked those in the spreadsheet; if you want us to propose redline language we'll loop in Legal (copying Karthik on next step).

Would you like a short walkthrough call tomorrow to review the templates and the SLA table? I can have Neha present the comms cadence and Marissa can walk the escalation flow.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
